page: Microsoft Azure D48plds_v5 is an ARM-based virtual machine powered by a 3.0 GHz Ampere Neoverse-N1 processor featuring 48 dedicated physical cores and 48 vCPUs. It is configured with 96.0 GB of memory, yielding a 2.0 GB per-core allocation suitable for compute-intensive tasks with lower memory overhead. The instance includes 1843 GB of local SSD storage and operates under the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The CPU architecture includes L1d cache of 64 KB, L2 cache of 1.0 MB per core, and 32 MB of shared L3 cache, with ARM AES cryptographic extensions enabled.

In benchmark testing, the server demonstrates strong multi-core scalability, earning top-tier results in multi-threaded CPU stress operations, Clang software compilation, and Redis SET throughput reaching 62.24 million operations per second. Conversely, single-threaded execution and text processing perform in lower benchmark brackets, emphasizing its reliance on core parallelism. Memory bandwidth and small-to-medium large language model inference speeds fall within average baseline ranges.

The D48plds_v5 provides strong qualitative cost efficiency for highly parallelized workloads by delivering high physical core density and integrated local SSD storage without charging for excessive RAM overhead. Its operational profile makes it best suited for continuous integration software build nodes, ARM-native web serving, key-value caching stores, and distributed microservices.
description: Microsoft Azure D48plds_v5 is an ARM-based compute-optimized virtual machine featuring 48 dedicated Ampere Neoverse-N1 physical cores running at 3.0 GHz without hyperthreading. It is provisioned with 96.0 GB of RAM (2.0 GB per core) and includes 1843 GB of local SSD storage. Designed for high multi-core throughput, the server demonstrates strong benchmark performance in multi-threaded CPU stress tests, software compilation with Clang, and Redis SET operations processing 62.24 million operations per second. Single-core performance and text processing benchmarks are weaker, reflecting the architecture's reliance on core parallelism over single-threaded speed. Cost efficiency is driven by high physical core density and direct local NVMe SSD capacity relative to its memory allocation. The D48plds_v5 is best suited for parallelized build environments, scale-out web applications, caching tiers, and microservices workloads optimized for ARM64 execution.
